sketches.title: The Fete That Nearly Held Together
sketches.premise: A gust has just hit the village fete. Take turns adding one repair to the same rescue plan: keep the stalls, people, and prizes safe while the weather gets worse. Make the plan work, but spend your partner’s time, pride, money, or dignity whenever you can.
sketches.criterion: A move holds if it adds exactly one workable next step that fits every fact in the plan; a skipped link is an unexplained jump, an ending is a finished rescue that leaves no next step, and an undo is cancelling or replacing an earlier repair.
sketches.move_shape: Add one linked action, naming who does it and what it fixes: “Mara ties the raffle tent to the mayor’s van with the bunting rope.”
sketches.first_card: The first gust lifts the cake tent, and the raffle tickets are blowing toward the duck pond.

sketches.title: And Now, A Small Disaster
sketches.premise: You are live-commentating a village fete as the first gust sends everything wobbling. Take turns adding exactly one beat to the same running commentary, making the scene clearer, funnier, and more awkward without jumping ahead. Earn points by making your partner explain, apologise, or look like a total muppet.
sketches.criterion: A move holds if it follows directly from the whole commentary and adds one new visible beat; a skipped link is a sudden change with no cause, an ending is a final wrap-up, and an undo is denying or rewriting a beat already reported.
sketches.move_shape: Add one immediate on-air beat: “The treasurer grabs the microphone, says ‘bugger,’ and loses his hat into the tombola.”
sketches.first_card: The fete opens under a grey sky, and the first gust sends the bunting snapping above the cake stall.

sketches.title: The Longest Slice of Cake
sketches.premise: The wind has knocked the cake stall sideways, and one cake must be passed safely from table to table before it falls apart. Take turns adding one hand-off or support to the same chain. Score for making your partner handle the mess, the blame, or an increasingly ridiculous cake problem.
sketches.criterion: A move holds if the cake can physically reach the named person or place from the full chain so far; a skipped link is a missing hand-off, an ending is putting the cake safely down, and an undo is moving it back or removing a support already used.
sketches.move_shape: Add one physical link: “Nell slides the cake board to Rob, who catches the loose corner with both elbows.”
sketches.first_card: The wind lifts the tablecloth, and the fete’s tallest sponge is sliding toward the edge of the cake table.

sketches.title: The Fete Lost Property Desk
sketches.premise: The first gust scatters odd things across the village fete. Build one shared lost-and-found trail, placing each new item somewhere it could really have gone and using the clues already given. Score when your partner must identify, carry, confess to, or be publicly blamed for the item.
sketches.criterion: A move holds if it places or identifies exactly one item using the whole clue trail; a skipped link is an unexplained location jump, an ending is declaring the search solved, and an undo is taking back an item’s established place or owner.
sketches.move_shape: Add one clue or discovery: “Under the jam table, Priya finds the judge’s false teeth inside the lucky-dip bucket.”
sketches.first_card: The first gust sends napkins, raffle slips, and one heavy-looking black bag skittering across the fete.

sketches.title: The Emergency Fete Meeting
sketches.premise: The wind has turned the village fete into a committee emergency. Take turns adding one motion to the same meeting, building a plan from the chair’s question through debate to a vote. Score for forcing your partner to defend a silly idea, admit a mistake, or volunteer for a grim job.
sketches.criterion: A move holds if it is the next sensible meeting step and answers what has already been raised; a skipped link is a motion appearing without being proposed, an ending is the final decision, and an undo is reopening or reversing a settled vote.
sketches.move_shape: Add one meeting step: “After Pam objects to using the church bell, the chair asks who will climb the tower and fetch the loudspeaker.”
sketches.first_card: The first gust tears down the fete map, and the chair calls an emergency meeting beside the wobbling bandstand.

sketches.title: The Prize Nobody Meant to Win
sketches.premise: The first gust blows open the fete prize bag, revealing a trail of prizes, notes, and suspicious swaps. Take turns adding one clue to the same mystery, keeping each new fact able to follow from the last. Score by making your partner look guilty, explain a terrible choice, or claim a prize they absolutely should not want.
sketches.criterion: A move holds if it adds one clue that fits the entire mystery and leaves a fair next question; a skipped link is an unsupported leap, an ending is naming the culprit and motive, and an undo is retracting or replacing an established clue.
sketches.move_shape: Add one clue: “The wet note inside the coconut says, ‘Meet behind the toilets,’ in handwriting that looks exactly like Len’s.”
sketches.first_card: The first gust flips the prize table, and among the fallen toys lies a sealed envelope marked WINNER: MRS BELL.
